# Instructions for accurately documenting failed electrical appliance safety checks

1. Start with the test records.
2.
completion:
document the date and time of the safety check.
 
3. Record the identity of the appliance: include its make, model, serial number, and any unique identifiers.

4. Identify the specific individual (name and qualifications) who conducted the safety check.

5. Describe the testing equipment and tools used: include their model numbers and calibration dates if applicable.

6. Provide a detailed description of the testing procedure followed: reference the relevant safety standards and protocols.

7. Note any pre-test observations: unusual sounds, smells, visible damage, previous repair records, etc.

8. Record the test results accurately, with precise measurements and readings. Use a standardized checklist if available.

9. Clearly indicate which safety tests failed, specifying the nature of each failure. For example, wiring issues, overheating, short-circuiting, frayed cords, malfunctioning switches, or non-compliance with safety standards.
